subject: Private deployment: module orchestration & CI handshake for private stack

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Cc: alice.tan@acme-robotics.com
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: module orchestration & CI handshake for private stack

Hi team,

Quick summary: Acme is seeing intermittent deploy failures during the private stack rollout that look like module ordering + CI orchestration race conditions (Terraform apply -> Helm hooks -> Ansible post-config). They have a narrow maintenance window next week and need a deterministic handshake between modules so their runbook can be automated.

I attached a compatibility matrix and a small patch that proposes an explicit "orchestration-handshake" CI job which enforces the sequence and validates transitional state. Key asks:
- Marissa: can we confirm this job is non-blocking for existing Dedicated customers?
- Irene: can you review the Ansible secret propagation note in the patch (lines ~45-62) — I think we need idempotent propagation rather than a push-only hook.
- Karthik: can you run a quick simulation with the enclave network egress checks enabled (INFRA-1283) and note any timing blowups?

Attachments: module-compat-matrix.csv, ci-pipeline-handshake.patch (patch shows added job + gating).

Proposed timeline: we get signoff by EOD Thu (4/9), run a staged canary on Friday in the Acme staging VLAN, and then schedule the maintenance window for next Tuesday.

Thanks — attaching the patch and matrix for quick review.

Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Sergio — thanks for the concise summary and the artifacts. I skimmed the patch and matrix. High-level notes:

- The handshake job looks reasonable as a preflight gate that runs after terraform plan/apply but before helm release. If we implement it as a pipeline-level stage (not repository-level), it can be toggled per-account which addresses the Dedicated vs hosted concern.
- We need to ensure the handshake job emits the same telemetry we show in the Console (tokens/latency per-route) so Acme's SREs can correlate failures with model routing changes.
- Non-blocking suggestion: run the handshake in "warn" mode for the first two runs (record results, don't fail pipeline). If results are clean, flip to blocking.

I attached a small CI run matrix I've used before for canaries (ci-run-matrix.csv) — use that as the initial set.

I'll take ownership of adding the pipeline toggle and telemetry emission. Need a quick test harness from Irene for Ansible behavior.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Private deployment: module orchestration & CI handshake for private stack

Thanks — quick technical read here. A couple of concerns and clarifications:

1) Ansible secret propagation: the patch uses a push-hook that copies secrets to vault -> consumer. For on-prem/private (especially air-gapped), we should avoid a push model. I propose making the module publish a signed artifact that the consumer module pulls and validates. That keeps idempotency and allows retries without double-writing secrets.

2) Helm hooks timing: helm pre-upgrade hooks currently run concurrently for multiple charts when we do umbrella releases. The handshake should explicitly serialize chart upgrades for charts that own the same CRDs or node-level network config. We can implement a lightweight mutex using a shared ConfigMap lock with TTL.

3) Test harness: I'll spin up a small staging run in the Acme VLAN that exercises the secret-pull flow and the ConfigMap lock. Sergio — can you provide the exact subnet / canary namespace for Acme staging? Alice — if you can open the maintenance window for ~45 minutes on Friday that will give us enough runs.

I added inline comments to the patch (see ci-pipeline-handshake.patch lines ~120-145) about rollback semantics.

Irene Choi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

All — thanks for the rapid reviews. I ran a short timing simulation against INFRA-1283 with the egress checks enabled. Results: when the network egress probes are enabled, we saw helm hook timing skew of ~6–9s per chart under a 200 concurrent-request spike. That can push a previously safe 2-minute window into a flaky state.

Action items I can take immediately:
- Add a per-module backoff jitter (configurable via module var) to the handshake job so the lock acquisition is less contended.
- Gate the blocking behavior behind the "warn" -> "fail" toggle Marissa suggested and default to warn for Acme for the first two runs.

Sergio — provide me the exact canary namespace and I'll run the harness (Irene's secret-pull + configmap-lock) on Friday morning and post the raw logs to the Drive folder. If results look stable, Marissa, please flip the toggle and we'll proceed with the maintenance window.

Karthik Iyer
Network & Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
